NORTHGATE CANCER CENTRE - CHEMOTHERAPY DAY UNIT
Systemic Anti-Cancer Therapy (SACT) - Patient Cycle Plan

Patient: Margaret OKAFOR     DOB: 14/02/1961     Hosp No: NG4471902
Consultant: Dr P. Raman (Medical Oncology)     Chemo nurse: Bev Allardyce
Regimen: CAPOX (capecitabine + oxaliplatin) - adjuvant, colon ca
Cycle length 21 days.  THIS PLAN = CYCLE 3 of 8
Ht 164 cm  Wt 71.2 kg  BSA 1.79 m2   Dose level: 85% (reduced after C2 diarrhoea)

DAY    DATE        WHAT HAPPENS
D-2    Mon 02/11   Pre-chemo bloods (FBC, U&E, LFT) - Phlebotomy, Level 1, 09:40
D1     Wed 04/11   Oxaliplatin 200 mg IV over 2 hrs - Day Unit chair 6, arrive 08:30
D1-D14             Capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily (BD) = 3 x 500mg tabs AM and 3 x 500mg tabs PM
D15-D21            NO capecitabine - rest week
D22    Wed 25/11   Cycle 4 Day 1 (if bloods OK)

Capecitabine: swallow whole with water within 30 mins after breakfast and evening meal, approx 12 hrs apart.
Last dose of this cycle = evening of D14 (Tue 17/11). Return any left over tablets to pharmacy.
Missed dose: do NOT double up. Skip it and take the next dose at the normal time.

ANTI-SICKNESS
Dexamethasone 8 mg once daily in the morning - D2 and D3 only (take with food)
Ondansetron 8 mg twice a day D1 to D3, then only if needed
Metoclopramide 10 mg up to 3 times a day if sick (as required)

- diarrhoea 4 or more times a day above your normal: STOP capecitabine and phone the hotline
- mouth ulcers: mouthwash after meals, phone if you cant eat or drink

Do not wait until the morning. Do not take paracetamol before you have rung.

LAKESIDE PEDIATRICS - Fever Care Plan
Patient: Ava Martinez     Age: 3 yrs     Weight: 33 lb (15 kg)
Date: 10/19/2026     Seen by: Jenna Cole, CPNP

Dx: viral illness with fever. Ears and lungs clear today, strep + flu swabs negative.
The goal is comfort, not a normal number. Treat the fever if she is uncomfortable or temp is over 102.2 F.

MEDICINES - use the dosing syringe that comes with each bottle, not a kitchen spoon
- Acetaminophen (Children's Tylenol) 160 mg/5 mL: give 7 mL (224 mg) every 6 hours as needed. Max 4 doses in 24 hrs.
- Ibuprofen (Children's Motrin) 100 mg/5 mL: give 7.5 mL (150 mg) every 6 hours as needed, with food or milk. Max 4 doses in 24 hrs.
If the fever comes back before the same medicine is due again, you may ALTERNATE: give the other medicine 3 hours after the last dose.

Example alternating schedule (if needed):
8:00 AM  - Tylenol 7 mL
11:00 AM - Motrin 7.5 mL
2:00 PM  - Tylenol 7 mL
5:00 PM  - Motrin 7.5 mL
8:00 PM  - Tylenol 7 mL
11:00 PM - Motrin 7.5 mL
2:00 AM  - Tylenol 7 mL
5:00 AM  - Motrin 7.5 mL
Write down every dose and the time on the log on the back so nobody double doses.
Once 1 medicine is keeping her comfortable, stop alternating. Don't wake her up just to give medicine.

Fluids: small sips often (water, Pedialyte, popsicles). Expect at least 4 wet diapers/pull-ups a day.
Fever usually lasts 2-3 days with a virus.

CALL US or go to the ER if:
* temp 104 F or higher, or fever lasting more than 3 days (past Thu 10/22)
* fast or hard breathing, very sleepy / hard to wake, stiff neck, rash that doesnt fade when pressed
* no wet diaper in 8 hours, or she can't keep fluids down

Office (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm): (614) 555-0182
After-hours nurse line (24/7): (614) 555-0199
Follow up: only if not improving - no visit booked.

HEPATITIS C TREATMENT PLAN

Name: Daniel Kemp      MRN: 20441876      DOB: 03/09/1984
Prescriber: Dr Lucy Tran (GP)     Hep C nurse: Sam Whitlock
PBS script - 2 x 28 day packs dispensed by Riverbend Pharmacy

PRE-TREATMENT RESULTS

Genotype: 3a
FibroScan 6.1 kPa (F0-F1, no cirrhosis)   APRI 0.42
ALT 88 U/L (mildly raised)   eGFR >90   Hep B sAg neg, HIV neg

YOUR MEDICINE
Maviret (glecaprevir 100 mg / pibrentasvir 40 mg) tablets
Take 3 tablets together ONCE a day WITH FOOD, at the same time each day.
Course: 8 weeks (56 days). Each box = 28 days (4 weekly cartons of 21 tablets).
Start: Mon 07/09/2026
Finish: Sun 01/11/2026 (last day of tablets)
Swallow whole, dont crush, chew or split them.

Missed dose:
- Less than 18 hrs since your usual time: take the 3 tablets as soon as you remember (with food), then the next dose at your usual time.
- More than 18 hrs: skip the missed dose and take the next one at the usual time. Do NOT take a double dose.
- Vomit within 3 hrs of a dose: take another 3 tablets. Vomit after 3 hrs: no extra dose needed.

INTERACTIONS - check with Sam or the pharmacist before starting anything new
- NO St John's Wort, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin
- atorvastatin / simvastatin - stop during treatment (Dr Tran)
- antacids, paracetamol, methadone - ok

FOLLOW UP

SVR12 blood test (the "cure" test): 12 weeks after finishing = from 24/01/2027. Pathology collection, form attached, no appointment needed.

EYE DROP CHART after cataract surgery

Operated eye: RIGHT (R)     Surgery date: Thu 08 Oct 2026
Surgeon: Mr D. Achterberg     Lens: +21.5 D monofocal

documents.text:
PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE USER
Levonorgestrel 150 microgram / Ethinylestradiol 30 microgram coated tablets
Read all of this leaflet carefully before you start taking this medicine. Keep it, you may need to read it again.

3. How to take this medicine
Take one tablet every day at about the same time, for 21 days, following the arrows on the strip.
Then have 7 tablet-free days (your "pill-free week"). You will usually have a withdrawal bleed during this week.
Start your next strip on day 8, even if you are still bleeding.

Starting for the first time
- Take your first tablet on day 1 of your period. You are protected straight away.
- If you start on day 2 to 5 of your period, also use condoms for the first 7 days.

If you forget to take a tablet
ONE tablet missed (less than 48 hours since you should have taken it):
- Take the missed tablet as soon as you remember, even if this means taking 2 tablets at the same time.
- Take the rest of the strip as usual. You are still protected. No extra contraception needed.

TWO OR MORE tablets missed (48 hours or more since you should have taken one):
- Take the most recent missed tablet as soon as you remember, even if this means taking 2 at once. Leave any earlier missed tablets.
- Carry on with the rest of the strip as usual and use condoms (or don't have sex) for the next 7 days.
- If 7 or more tablets are left in the strip after the missed ones: finish the strip and have your normal 7-day break.
- If fewer than 7 tablets are left: finish the strip and start the next strip the next day WITHOUT a break.
- If you missed tablets in the first week of the strip and had unprotected sex in the pill-free week or in that first week, you may need emergency contraception. Speak to a pharmacist or doctor.

If you are sick or have diarrhoea
- Vomiting within 2 hours of taking a tablet: take another tablet as soon as you feel well enough, as if it were a missed tablet.
- Severe diarrhoea for more than 24 hours: follow the missed tablet advice above.

Stop taking this medicine and see a doctor at once if you notice:
- pain or swelling in one leg, sudden chest pain or breathlessness
- a severe headache unlike your usual ones, or sudden problems with your sight or speech

Storage: do not store above 25C. Keep out of the sight and reach of children.

COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH TEAM (NORTH) - LITHIUM TREATMENT PLAN
Patient: Priya Sandhu     DOB: 11/06/1990     NHS No: 612 448 9031
Psychiatrist: Dr H. Obi     Care co-ordinator: Mark Ellis (CPN)
Plan agreed: 28/09/2026 (copy to GP, Ashfield Medical Practice)

Medicine: PRIADEL (lithium carbonate) modified-release tablets, 200 mg and 400 mg
Always get the same brand (Priadel). Do not switch brands without talking to us. Carry your purple lithium card.

DOSE PLAN - take ONCE a day at NIGHT (about 21:00)
Step 1 from 28/09/2026: 400 mg at night (1 x 400 mg tablet)
Step 2 from 06/10/2026: 600 mg at night (1 x 400 mg + 1 x 200 mg tablet)
Step 3 only if level still under 0.6: 800 mg at night - Dr Obi will ring you to confirm first

LITHIUM BLOOD LEVELS
- Blood must be taken 12 hours after your night dose = 09:00 the next morning. Take your night dose as normal the evening before.
- Level 1 week after starting and 1 week after every dose change, weekly until 2 levels in a row are in range.
- Then every 3 months for the first year (kidney + thyroid + calcium every 6 months).
- Target range: 0.6 - 0.8 mmol/L

RESULTS SO FAR
05/10/2026   0.38 mmol/L   (on 400 mg)   below range -> increased to 600 mg
13/10/2026   0.57 mmol/L   (on 600 mg)   just under - stay on 600 mg, recheck in 1 week
Next level: Tue 20/10/2026 at 09:00, Millfield Health Centre phlebotomy (ground floor)
Baseline 25/09/2026: eGFR 98, TSH 1.9, adj Ca 2.31, wt 68 kg, ECG normal

MISSED DOSE: if you remember before midnight, take it then. If later, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. Never take 2 doses together.
Drink 2-3 litres of fluid a day, more in hot weather or if exercising. Dont suddenly cut down on salt.
Avoid ibuprofen, naproxen and other anti-inflammatories (they push the level up) - paracetamol is fine.
Tell any doctor, dentist or pharmacist that you are on lithium.

SIGNS OF TOO MUCH LITHIUM - stop taking it and get help the same day:
coarse shaking, being sick, diarrhoea, unsteady walking, slurred speech, muscle twitching, confusion

Out of hours: Crisis Team 0300 123 4567, or NHS 111

BRIGHTWATER ORAL & MAXILLOFACIAL SURGERY
Post-Op Instructions - Wisdom Teeth Removal

Patient: Tyler Brooks     Date of surgery: 10/16/2026
Procedure: extraction #1, #16, #17, #32 (all 4 wisdom teeth), IV sedation
Surgeon: Dr. Renee Whitfield, DDS

FIRST 24 HOURS
- Bite firmly on the gauze for 30-45 min. Change it every 30 min if still bleeding.
- Ice packs on the cheeks 20 min on / 20 min off for the first 36 hrs
- No spitting, no straws, no smoking/vaping for at least 72 hrs (dry socket!!)
- Do not rinse today. Starting tomorrow: warm salt water rinse (1/2 tsp salt in 8 oz water) after meals and at bedtime.

MEDICATIONS
Amoxicillin 500 mg: take 1 capsule 3 times a day (about every 8 hrs) until ALL are gone - 21 capsules = 7 days. Do not stop early even if you feel fine.
If the antibiotic upsets your stomach, take it with food. Call us if you get a rash, hives or bad diarrhea.
Ibuprofen 600 mg: 1 tablet every 6 hours with food for the first 3 days, then only as needed. No more than 4 tablets (2400 mg) in 24 hrs.
Acetaminophen (Tylenol) 500 mg: 2 tablets (1000 mg) every 6 hours - can be staggered with the ibuprofen (ex: ibuprofen 8am, Tylenol 11am, ibuprofen 2pm...). Max 3000 mg a day.
Chlorhexidine 0.12% rinse: 15 mL, swish 30 sec and spit gently, twice daily starting day 3, for 1 week.
On birth control pills? Use a backup method while on the antibiotic and for 7 days after.

DIET
Cool soft foods day 1 (yogurt, smoothies with a spoon, applesauce). Advance as tolerated. No seeds, chips or rice for 1 week.

CALL THE OFFICE IF
- bleeding that wont slow down after 2 sets of gauze
- fever over 101 F, or swelling getting WORSE after day 3
- pain getting worse on day 3-5 (could be dry socket)

Suture check / post-op visit: Fri 10/23/2026 at 3:45 PM (dissolvable stitches, quick check)
Office: (503) 555-0147     After hours on-call surgeon: (503) 555-0160

PADDINGTON PAWS VETERINARY HOSPITAL
Discharge Instructions & Medication Sheet

Patient: "Bella"   Canine - Labrador X, F/S, 9 yrs   Weight: 26.4 kg
Owner: Nicole Fraser     Vet: Dr Tom Hadley BVSc     Date: Sat 17/10/2026
Presenting: lame R hind (osteoarthritis R stifle on x-ray) + superficial pyoderma on belly/inner thighs

MEDICATIONS
1. Carprofen (Rimadyl) 100 mg chewable tablets - anti-inflammatory/pain relief
Give 1 tablet ONCE a day WITH FOOD (breakfast). 30 tabs supplied.
2. Cephalexin (Rilexine) 600 mg tablets - antibiotic for the skin
Give 1 tablet TWICE a day (approx every 12 hrs, e.g. 7am + 7pm) for 21 days. Finish the whole course even if the skin looks better.
3. Gabapentin 100 mg capsules - extra pain relief
Give 3 capsules (300 mg) at night if she is sore or restless. May make her a bit wobbly/sleepy.
4. Malaseb medicated shampoo - wash belly twice weekly, leave on 10 min then rinse well.

MISSED DOSE: give it when you remember, unless it is nearly time for the next dose - then skip the missed one. Never give a double dose.
STOP the carprofen and call us if she vomits, has diarrhoea, black/tarry poo, stops eating, or her gums/eyes look yellow.
Do not give any human pain meds (ibuprofen, Nurofen, Panadol, aspirin) - can be very dangerous for dogs.

Exercise: lead walks only, 2-3 short walks (15-20 min) a day for 2 weeks. No ball chasing or jumping off the couch/ute.
Weight: target 24 kg - cut her dinner by 1/4 cup, no extra treats. Feed her in a seperate room from the other dog.
Cone (e-collar) if she licks the belly. Hydrotherapy referral given.

RECHECK: Sat 07/11/2026 at 9:30am with Dr Hadley (skin + leg)
Before any repeat carprofen script: blood test (liver/kidney) - can be done at the recheck, no fasting needed.

Formula Feeding Plan - Baby Isla (born 02/09/2026)
From: Maternal & Child Health nurse visit 14/10/2026
Weight today 5.1 kg (birth 3.4 kg) - tracking nicely along the 50th centile

Formula: Stage 1 infant formula (0-6 months)
Mixing: 1 level scoop to every 30 ml of cooled boiled water. Water FIRST, then powder.
Never add extra scoops "to fill her up" - too strong is hard on her kidneys.

Feed every 3 hours during the day, let her sleep longer overnight if she wants (max 5 hrs between feeds at this age).
Amount: about 150 ml per feed, 6-7 feeds in 24 hrs (approx 900-1000 ml a day)

TIME      AMOUNT    NOTES
6:00am    150 ml    5 scoops
9:00am    150 ml    5 scoops
12:00pm   150 ml    tummy time after
3:00pm    150 ml
6:00pm    150 ml    bath before this one
9:00pm    180 ml    "dream feed" - 6 scoops
3:00am    150 ml    only if she wakes

If she skips or sleeps through a feed, just offer the next one at the normal amount - don't double up or squeeze 2 feeds into one bottle.
Throw out any formula left in the bottle after 1 hour.
Made-up bottles: back of the fridge (not the door), use within 24 hrs.
Wet nappies: 6+ heavy ones a day = she's drinking enough.
Burp halfway thru and at the end. Hold her upright 10-15 min after if she's spilling.

POOL CARE LOG - 14 Banksia Cres (in-ground, fibreglass)
Volume: 45,000 L     Sanitiser: liquid chlorine + stabiliser
Targets: FC 2-4 ppm | pH 7.2-7.6 | TA 80-120 ppm | CYA 30-50 ppm | CH 200-300 ppm

WEEKLY ROUTINE (every Saturday morning, before anyone swims)
1. Test with the drop kit + strips, write results below
2. Skim, empty the skimmer basket + pump basket
3. Brush walls/steps, vac if needed
4. Dose chemicals - pump running, add in front of a return jet, one chemical at a time, wait 4 hrs between

DOSING GUIDE (for 45,000 L)
Liquid chlorine 12.5%: 1 L raises FC approx 2.8 ppm. Usual top-up 2 L weekly (summer 3-4 L, twice weekly)
Shock (cal hypo granules 65%): 450 g once a week in summer, fortnightly in winter. Dissolve in a bucket of pool water first.
pH down (dry acid): 200 g lowers pH by about 0.2. Max 400 g per dose.
Buffer (sodium bicarb): 1.2 kg raises TA approx 15 ppm
Stabiliser (CYA): 450 g raises CYA approx 10 ppm - only if under 30, takes a week to dissolve in the skimmer sock

DATE    FC    pH    TA    CYA   ADDED
03/10   1.5   7.8   110   40    2 L chlorine, 200 g dry acid
10/10   2.0   7.6   100   40    2 L chlorine
17/10   1.0   7.9   100   35    3 L chlorine, 400 g dry acid, 450 g shock (hot wk, lots of swimmers)
24/10

Wait 1 hr after liquid chlorine before swimming, 8 hrs after shock (do it at dusk, swim next morning).
AquaBlue Pool Supplies does a free water test on Saturdays - bring a 500 ml sample taken from elbow deep.
Cartridge filter clean: every 6 weeks, last done 26/09, next ~07/11. Spare cartridge in the shed.
Robot vac runs Tue + Fri 3 hrs (timer on the power board).

documents.name: pale_ale_batch14_recipe.txt
documents.text:
Bench Seat Pale Ale - all grain, BIAB     Batch #14
Batch size 23 L into fermenter | OG 1.050 target | FG 1.011 | ~5.2% ABV | ~38 IBU

GRAIN BILL
Pale malt (Maris Otter)   4.50 kg
Munich I                  0.50 kg
Crystal 40L               0.25 kg
Wheat malt                0.20 kg

MASH: 32 L strike water @ 72C -> mash 66C for 60 min. Mash out 76C 10 min.
Water: Campden 1/2 tab in strike water. Gypsum 5 g + CaCl 3 g in the mash.

BOIL 60 min (pre-boil ~28 L)
60 min     Magnum 14% AA   15 g
15 min     Cascade         20 g + Whirlfloc 1/2 tab + yeast nutrient 1/2 tsp
0 min / whirlpool 80C 20 min: Cascade 30 g, Centennial 20 g

FERMENT
Chill to 18C. Yeast: US-05, 1 sachet (11.5 g), rehydrate in 100 ml water at 25-30C for 15 min.
Day 1-6: hold 18C
Day 7: dry hop Cascade 40 g + Citra 30 g (in a bag), let it free rise to 20C
Day 10: check gravity, again day 12 - if the same both days its done
Day 12-14: cold crash 2C for 2 days

PACKAGING
Bottles: priming sugar (dextrose) 6 g per litre of beer -> 21 L = 126 g, dissolved in 200 ml boiled water, cooled.
Condition bottles at 20C+ for 2 weeks, then fridge 3-5 days before drinking.
Keg: 2 days @ 300 kPa (40 psi) then down to 80 kPa to serve.

Notes: last batch (#13) finished at 1.014, a bit sweet - mash 1C lower this time.
Sanitise EVERYTHING after the boil (Starsan 1.5 ml per litre, no rinse).

documents.name: monstera_care_card.txt
documents.text:
PLANT CARE CARD - Monstera deliciosa (Swiss cheese plant)
Green Thumb Nursery & Garden Centre  |  Pot size: 250 mm

LIGHT: bright indirect light. No harsh afternoon sun (leaves scorch).
WATER: water weekly in spring/summer - when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry. Every 2 weeks in winter.
Water thoroughly until it drains out the bottom, then empty the saucer after 30 min.
FEEDING: feed monthly Sept-March with liquid fertiliser, 5 ml per litre of water. Don't feed Apr-Aug.
Never feed a dry plant - water first, then feed.
HUMIDITY: likes 60%+. Mist the leaves 2-3 times a week, or sit it on a pebble tray.
TEMP: 18-27C ideal. Keep above 12C. Away from heater/aircon vents.
CLEANING: wipe the leaves with a damp cloth monthly.
REPOTTING: every 2 years in spring, one size up (50 mm bigger). Use aroid mix (bark + perlite + potting mix 1:1:1).
SUPPORT: add a moss pole when it starts to lean - ties every 20-30 cm.

PESTS: check under the leaves fortnightly for mealybug, spider mite, thrips.
Treat: wipe or spray with eco-oil or neem (10 ml per litre), every 7 days x 3 treatments.

TOXIC TO PETS + CHILDREN if chewed (calcium oxalate). Keep away from cats/dogs.

Yellow lower leaf = usually overwatering. Brown crispy edges = low humidity or underwatering.
Recomended: rotate the pot a quarter turn each month so it grows evenly.
Questions? Pop in or call (07) 5555 2190, open 7 days 8am-5pm
